newsitem.title: FRANCE: Best French barley bid seen covering 10,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Best French barley bid seen covering 10,000 tonnes.

text.p: The lowest subsidy bid for barley in France on Thursday -- at 14.49 Ecus -- covered 10,000 tonnes out of a total 153,700 tonnes sought, grain traders estimated.

However, some traders disagreed with earlier estimates of the world price implied by this bid, saying the best domestic buying prices quoted on the market were currently only workable for tiny volumes, and not for export-sized shipments.
A domestic price of 855 francs per tonne, delivered Rouen for May and excluding carrying charges, traded on Wednesday but only for about 500 tonnes of barley, traders said.
One estimated a more realistic price for larger quantities at closer to 860 or 865 francs per tonne, although the market had yet to turn this into practice.
The higher price, plus a late-May carrying charge of 72.71 francs per tonne, would equate to about $152 per tonne fob at refund of 14.49 Ecus rather than the $150 initially estimated.
Further up the scale for refunds, traders said a combined total of 45,000 tonnes was sought at a maximum subsidy of 15.50 Ecus. The tonnage includes the lower bids at 14.49 Ecus.
Other cumulative totals were seen as follows -- 76,000 tonnes at refunds up to 16.00 Ecus, 113,000 tonnes at a maximum 16.90 Ecus and 153,700 tonnes at refunds up to 19.94 Ecus.
The cut-off level of 16 Ecus was seen worth around $151. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
